info.name: Employee Management API
info.description:
Secure Employee Management System (Express 5 + PostgreSQL). Run the whole collection in order (Collection Runner or `npx newman run`) against a freshly seeded database: `npm run db:seed`.

Folders: authentication, employees, departments, unauthenticated/invalid requests, the three final-challenge attack scenarios, and sign-out. Every request has tests; every response must carry an X-Request-Id header (collection-level test).

The refresh token travels in an HttpOnly cookie, which Postman stores in its cookie jar automatically. Seeded accounts and their development password are listed in the README.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Login for each role, generic login errors, refresh rotation, sessions.

exec: pm.test('no password hash or password in the response', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/argon2|password_?hash/i));
pm.test('refresh token is NOT in the body', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property('refreshToken'));
pm.test('refresh cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict', () => { const c = pm.response.headers.get('Set-Cookie'); pm.expect(c).to.include('HttpOnly'); pm.expect(c).to.include('SameSite=Strict'); });

item.name: Login with an unknown email → same 401

exec: pm.test('same message as a wrong password (no account enumeration)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('invalidLoginMessage')));

item.name: Refresh the access token (rotates the cookie)

exec: pm.test('the current session is marked', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().items.some((s) => s.current)).to.be.true);

item.name: Create with a duplicate work email → 409
Create in a department that does not exist → 422
Create with an invalid body → structured 400
New hire changes their password (revokes all sessions)
The old access token no longer works → 401
Admin promotes the new hire to manager
Manager lists their team (direct reports only)
Manager reads someone outside their team → 404

4. Unauthenticated and invalid requests
item.description: What happens without valid credentials or input.

item.name: 5. Attack scenarios (final challenge)
item.description: The three attacks to demonstrate. Each must fail safely. See docs/security-report.md.

item.name: A1. Employee sends "role": "admin" to their own profile → 400

exec: pm.test('role is not an allowed field', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.details).to.deep.include({ path: 'body.role', message: 'is not an allowed field' }));

request.description: Control: strict request schema (src/validators/employee.validators.ts) rejects any field not on the allowlist.

item.name: A2. HR tries to make themselves admin → 403

request.description: Control: requireRole("admin") + requirePermission("user:assign-role") on /users, and canAssignRole() in UserService.

item.name: A3. HR logs in again: still "hr"
B1. Employee reads another employee by changing the id → 404

request.description: Control: employeeAccess() in EmployeeService; out-of-scope records answer 404, exactly like missing ones.

item.name: C1. Victim logs in (attacker copies the refresh token)
C3. Attacker replays the old token → 401, session revoked

request.description: Control: AuthService.refresh() sees the token was already used, revokes the whole token family (session) and writes a session.reuse_detected audit entry.

item.name: C4. The victim’s current refresh token is revoked too → 401
C5. And so is the access token of that session → 401
